questions.q: How does this lesson say a research question differs from a course assignment?
options: A research question comes with a known answer key, an assignment doesn't
A research question asks something you don't already know the answer to, and you decide what counts as evidence
There is no real difference, just different wording
A research question is always about machine learning specifically
questions.explain: An assignment tells you what to build and what correct looks like. A research question asks something unknown and commits you to finding out with evidence.

questions.q: Which of the following best passes this lesson's 'falsifiable' test?
options: "RL is interesting for database work"
"Does an RL agent choosing from six plan hints beat the optimizer's default plan on 200 held-out episodes?"
"SQL is a useful language"
"Machine learning will keep improving"
questions.explain: A falsifiable question names an experiment whose result could come out either way and would settle the claim — the Project 1 framing does exactly that.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does 'scoped to days, not months' matter?
options: Because longer projects are never worth doing
Because a question answerable in an afternoon is too small to be interesting, and one needing months of infrastructure is a different kind of team's job
Because the course platform enforces a hard deadline
Because days are easier to write down than months
questions.explain: The lesson frames days-not-months as the sweet spot: small enough to be practical, big enough to actually learn something, unlike projects at either extreme.

questions.q: What is Project 2's research question testing, as framed in this lesson?
options: Whether a reward model ranks the human-preferred cleaned record higher than the alternative
Whether an RL agent can clean Northwind data directly
Whether SQL Pete can answer natural-language questions
Whether activation patching reveals a circuit
questions.explain: Project 2's question is whether a distilbert-based reward model, trained on labeled pairs, ranks the human-preferred cleaned record higher — and where it fails.

questions.q: Which statement is NOT one of the lesson's three tests for a good research question?
options: Specific
Falsifiable
Scoped to days, not months
Peer-reviewed before you start
questions.explain: The three tests given are specific, falsifiable, and scoped to days rather than months. Peer review isn't one of them.
